newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bel-20 index bound for more glory.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bel-20 index bound for more glory.

text.p: Belgium's Bel-20 index is bound to continue its bull run on the back of a steady pile of cash lured to the share market by a favourable climate of low interest rates and the relatively strong dollar.

"We're not going to rise every day, but the basic trend will still be up," said analyst Stefan Casteleyn at Corluy & Co. "Every day new retail investors show up to transfer their cash into stocks," he said.
At 0830 GMT, the Bel-20 was up 0.29 percent, or 6.51 points, at 2,248.88 after earlier touching 2,252.40 following Wall Street's 123-point surge last night.
Casteleyn said that in the current climate any correction would be muted and shortlived.
"We had a correction and it didn't mean much," he said. "I'm glad we did sweat it out," he said.
Noting that the Bel-20 came tantalisingly close to his 1997 target of 2,300 points, he said that the brokerage continued to be fully-invested in European stocks -- "even at 2,300".
The share market would also be bolstered by a further drive towards restructuring in the corporate world.
In the short term, he expected some caution ahead of a batch of U.S. data later this week.
Oil company Petrofina was market leader in value terms, rising 0.6 percent to 12,875 francs.

Dealers said it was supported by the upcoming expiry of a warrant on its shares, which can be exercised until June 3, and comments by Petrofina CEO Francois Cornelis that earnings nearly doubled in the first four months of 1997.
"Petrofina is not one of our favourites but the profit figures really look good," Casteleyn said.
Generale Bank said in its daily equity comment it maintained its buy recommendation for Petrofina.
Casteleyn said he continued to recommend holding companies, most of which were still trading at a discount.
"Belgium is the land of holdings..and the big ones are still cleary at a discount," he said.
